decisions.reason: This classic lever line is close to the core range and costs little to keep, so even with no website mention in 2020 and 2021 the firm would likely leave it in the catalogue rather than formally withdraw it.
The firm has sunk tooling and catalogue investment across several models, and weak visibility can still be blamed on the pandemic slowdown in project specifications, so persistence is likely.
This single design is less entrenched and has not been mentioned since 2018, which raises the chance of quiet removal, but it fits the established offer and is cheap to keep.
This standalone handle design has little visible commitment behind it, but a German fittings maker rarely cuts a low-cost design that fits the range, so it stays for now.
This multi-model family carries sunk investment and supports the firm's announced push toward system breadth, so management would justify keeping it despite the lack of recent publicity.

The L700 is the publicly announced flagship of the firm's digital building strategy with heavy investment behind it, so management will persist and attribute any weak results to temporary market conditions.
